{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=examples+of+safety-critical+failures+caused+by+literal+interpretation+of+operator+instructions+in+autonomous+agent+deployment&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1515/9780748631131-009\", \"title\": [\"7 Literal Meaning in Modern Muslim Legal Theory: Two Examples\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1515/9780748631131-009\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2012, 7, 26]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.3720368\", \"title\": [\"Critical Analysis of Literal Rule of Interpretation\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.3720368\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2020]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7394258\", \"title\": [\"Autonomous Agent Reliability, Safety Auditing, and Action Fairness: A Systematic Review of Benchmarks, Execution Grounding, and Deployment Governance\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Large Language Model (LLM) and Vision-Language Model (VLM) agents now execute API calls, construct database queries, browse dynamic web interfaces, and trigger backend transactions inside production software systems. Because the consequential output of such a system is an executed action rather than a paragraph, static text benchmarks such as HELM leave several failure modes unmeasured: demographic bias in discrete tool selection, unhandled runtime exceptions, corrupted transaction state, cascading multi-agent delusion, and a measurement artifact that inflates apparent bias whenever the fairness null is computed at the wrong group arity. This review synthesizes 59 sources into four governance pillars. Under action-space fairness auditing we set out the Bias Conduction Framework, Counterfactual Flip Rates, Mean Absolute Score Disparity, and the extreme-value expansion E[∆ K ] ≈ 2σ √ 2 ln K that AgentFairBench adopts as its null, and we show that this asymptotic form is loose at audit-scale group counts, deriving an exact arity mismatch factor of 2.25× for a six-group audit scored against a two-run baseline. Resource-efficient safety screening on commodity CPUs (TriEval) forms the second pillar. The third contrasts open-loop scaffolds such as ReAct and Toolformer against closed-loop architectures enforcing Abstract Syntax Tree schema validation, sandboxed execution, and transactional rollback (ExecuGraph), while the fourth covers predeployment governance through class-conditional Mondrian conformal calibration and multi-metric pre-clearance gating (RISED). Instability on the scoring side cuts across all four, since paraphrase-induced verdict flips in LLM-as-a-judge pipelines corrupt the statistics these audits consume.
